draft.title: The government's economic objectives
card: The Australian Government sets economic objectives: goals it tries to reach through its decisions. The main aim is to keep living standards rising over time.
Steady economic growth
a rise in the total output of goods and services (the amount the economy produces) that is sustained over time, not one that jumps up and down.
Full employment
a situation where almost everyone who wants a job can find one. Some unemployment will always remain, for example people moving between jobs.
Stable prices
prices that rise slowly and predictably. Prices that rise quickly make money buy less, and make it hard for households and businesses to plan.
draft.remember: Steady growth, full employment and stable prices all aim to keep living standards rising.

a.q: Which of these is one of the Australian Government's economic objectives?
opts: Stable prices that rise slowly and predictably
Prices that fall each year for every good
A fixed number of jobs in each industry
Output that rises quickly in some years and falls in others
a.why: Stable prices means prices that rise slowly and predictably, which helps households and businesses plan. The option about output rising and falling describes the opposite of steady growth, which is sustained over time.
a.clue: Look for the goal that matches the three on the card.

b.q: Dev lives in Darwin and says: "The economy is doing well because we have full employment, so some people must still be unemployed." Why is his claim about unemployment wrong?
opts: Full employment still allows some people to be between jobs
Full employment means every person in Australia has a job
Full employment is only reached when prices stop rising
Full employment means the economy has stopped growing
b.why: Full employment means almost everyone who wants a job can find one, so a small amount of unemployment remains, such as people moving between jobs. It does not mean that every person has a job.
b.clue: Think about people who are changing jobs.

a.best: Stable prices that rise slowly and predictably

b.best: Full employment still allows some people to be between jobs

problems.detail: Dev's claim ('we have full employment, so some people must still be unemployed') is correct by the card's own definition, yet the question asks why it is wrong. The intended answer actually supports his claim, so the question contradicts the card and teaches confusion. Rewrite Dev's claim as something false, such as 'so no one is unemployed'.
The why says full employment 'does not mean that every person has a job', which answers a different claim from the one Dev makes. It contradicts the question stem.
The clue 'Think about people who are changing jobs' points straight at the only option that mentions being between jobs, which gives the answer away.

The right option is the only one that names an objective ('Stable prices') and copies the card's wording, and the clue tells students to match the card. A student could pick it without understanding the idea.

a.q: Over five years, the cost of a family's weekly grocery shop in Hobart goes up by a small, similar amount each year. Which objective does this show being met?
opts: Stable prices
Steady economic growth
Full employment
Fixed prices
a.why: The cost of goods is rising slowly and predictably, which is what stable prices means. Fixed prices is tempting, but it is not one of the government's objectives, and the costs here do change each year.
a.clue: Is this case about output, jobs or the cost of things?

b.q: Dev lives in Darwin and says: "We have full employment, so no one in Australia is unemployed." Is Dev right?
opts: No, some unemployment remains at full employment
Yes, full employment means every worker has a job
Yes, but only while prices stay stable each year
No, because full employment stops economic growth
b.why: Full employment means almost everyone who wants a job can find one, so a small amount of unemployment still remains, such as people moving between jobs. Saying every worker has a job is the common mistake: full employment does not mean zero unemployment.
b.clue: Does full employment cover every single person, or nearly everyone?

b.best: No, some unemployment remains at full employment
